# 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA)

- Principle: 1 Perceivable
- Guideline: 1.4 Distinguishable
- Level: AA
- Versions: 2.1, 2.2
- Understanding: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html
- Specification: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast

## Normative text

The visual [presentation](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-presentation) of the following have a [contrast ratio](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-contrast-ratio) of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s):

- **User Interface Components**

  Visual information required to identify [user interface components](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-user-interface-components) and [states](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-states), except for inactive components or where the appearance of the component is determined by the [user agent](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-user-agents) and not modified by the author;

- **Graphical Objects**

  Parts of graphics required to understand the content, except when a particular presentation of graphics is [essential](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-essential) to the information being conveyed.

## Sufficient techniques

- Situation A: Color is used to identify user interface components
  - Identifying user interface components using the following techniques:
    - G174: Providing a control with a sufficient contrast ratio that allows users to switch to a presentation that uses sufficient contrast
- Situation B: Color is used to identify a user interface component's focus state
  - Identifying a user interface component's focus state using the following techniques:
    - G195: Using an author-supplied, visible focus indicator
    - C40: Creating a two-color focus indicator to ensure sufficient contrast with all components
- Situation C: Color is required to understand graphical content
  - Making graphical content understandable using the following techniques:
    - G207: Ensuring that a contrast ratio of 3:1 is provided for icons
    - G209: Provide sufficient contrast at the boundaries between adjoining colors

## Failures

- F78: Failure of Success Criterion 1.4.11, 2.4.7 and 2.4.13 due to styling element outlines and borders in a way that removes or renders non-visible the visual focus indicator
